A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same CLAY research work and complete supplementary Sections A–F. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison; v2's additional page contains bibliography overflow.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval accuracy, runtime measurements, and component ablations in Tables 2–5, with additional experiments in supplementary Tables S6–S8.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including retrieval comparisons, timing experiments, ablations, and supplementary evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same textual subspace construction, tangent-space mapping, visual-feature rotation, and cosine-similarity inference. Algorithm 1 is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same real-world fine-grained datasets, CLEVR4, CLAY-EVAL, and GeneCIS Focus Attribute benchmark. Single-condition, multi-condition, and qualitative test scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding main and supplementary experiments, including GeneCIS, SEARLE, MagicLens, InstructBLIP, Qwen3-VL, VLM2Vec, and CIReVL. The newly cited concurrent work is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Both retain the same query/database splits, sample counts, model backbones, mAP and Recall@k metrics, and testing procedures. The timing comparison still uses a 100-image CLAY-Object database.

E4.justification: The rotation/manifold ablation in Table 5, backbone comparisons, singular-value analysis, and supplementary t-SNE and qualitative analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report average retrieval latency across 10 runs. Run and seed disclosures are unchanged, with no added confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 2–5 and S6–S8 and qualitative findings match. For example, CLAY with SigLIP-B retains 66.2 Stanford40 Action mAP in Table 2, and CLAY with CLIP-B retains 24.4 Recall@1 in Table S7.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(14), the tangent-space assumptions, and the Householder transformation construction are unchanged. No mathematical definition, derivation, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free conditional similarity, fixed visual embeddings, multi-condition retrieval, CLAY-EVAL, and accuracy–efficiency advantages.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning symmetric conditioning, rotation, manifold geometry, and rankability are retained. Appendix E preserves the limitations concerning multiple objects and attributes absent from the original visual representations.

D1.justification: Prompt templates, ChatGPT-5 usage, k = 50, FLUX generation parameters, dataset construction details, and access information remain unchanged. No additional implementation or reproducibility information is disclosed.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a sentence acknowledging concurrent work on constructing text-conditioned embedding spaces and cites Liu et al., Conditional representation learning for customized tasks, as reference 35. Existing cited works are retained under renumbering.

P1.justification: The related-work discussion gains one sentence, and the arXiv version/date header changes. The remaining prose and section sequence are retained, without substantial rewriting or reorganization.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is reduced in size, and existing text and table placement reflows. The final reference spills onto a nearly empty additional page. Figures, tables, and their substantive contents are otherwise retained, including in the appendices.

improvement.justification: Acknowledging similar concurrent research in Section 2 modestly improves attribution and research positioning. Methods, empirical support, and reproducibility remain unchanged. The smaller Figure 4 and nearly empty reference page introduce minor presentation costs, leaving the overall gain limited.
